article.headline: Zeta Global Rises 3.2% As Marketing Software Sales Jump 43.5%
article.deck: Zeta Global sits 1.9% past a 32.91 flat-base buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 34.56, with its RS line at a new high.
body: Zeta Global sells marketing software to big companies. Its cloud platform pulls together consumer data and uses it to find, win and keep customers, and its Zeta Messaging arm is an email service provider that sends AI-driven campaigns across channels. Clients use it to decide whom to reach, with what message and through which channel.

The sales line explains the stock. June-quarter revenue rose 43.5% to $442.8 million. Across the four quarters given, revenue climbed from $337.2 million to $394.6 million, $396.3 million and then $442.8 million. Earnings are thin and uneven: per-share results ran -0.02, 0.03, -0.05 and 0.03, and the June quarter's 3 cents a share is a profit. The next report is due Nov. 3.
The market values Zeta at $8.36 billion. With no trailing profit to measure, the stock has no trailing P/E; on forward estimates it trades at 27.9 times earnings.

Shares rose 1.05, or 3.2%, to 33.55 Tuesday on volume 0.93x the 50-day average. The stock broke out Oct. 5 from a four-week flat base that ran 14.6% deep, from a high on Sept. 4 to a low on Sept. 28; that session traded 1.17x its average. The buy point is 32.91 and the buy range runs to 34.56. Eleven sessions after the breakout, the close is 1.9% above the buy point and still in range.

The trend is orderly. The stock is 4.3% above its 21-day exponential average of 32.17, only 0.21 ATRs from the 21-day line, and 9.1% above its 50-day line at 30.76. The 200-day line is 51.8% below the close at 22.10. The close is 6.2% below the 52-week high of 35.75; the 52-week low is 14.36. Zeta holds an RS rank of 96 of 99 on the desk's list, its RS line is at a new high, and it is among the leaders of the desk's software group. The stock is up 64.9% this year, 66.3% over three months and 88.3% over 12 months.

The news has been steady. Zeta unveiled AthenaOS on Oct. 8 to connect AI, data and marketing workflows, and a headline the day before said it expanded its AI arsenal with a Digital Audience buyout. It named a new UK president as, a headline said, valuation questions linger. After the close Tuesday, TheStreet ran a headline saying Goldman sees 41% upside in an overlooked AI stock. After hours the shares were at 33.85, up 0.9%.
The Nov. 3 report puts the revenue run to its next test.
article.watch: The 34.56 top of the buy range and the Nov. 3 earnings report.

body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise rose 3.01, or 5.4%, to 59.10 in after-hours trading as of 6:15 p.m. ET. The payload's headlines carry no earnings report; the last report date listed was Sept. 2. At the close the stock was up 0.22, or 0.4%, at 56.09 on volume 0.66x its 50-day average, a session that left it 5.7% below its 50-day line at 59.45. Even the after-hours price sits under that line.

HPE broke out Oct. 1 past a 64.35 buy point from a 17-week deep cup that ran 36.6% deep, on volume 0.79x the average. Thirteen sessions later the close is 12.8% below the buy point, so the breakout has failed. The stock is 10.3% below its 21-day exponential average of 62.51 and -1.57 ATRs from the 21-day line, meaning the session's high stayed under it. The close is 23.7% below the 52-week high of 73.56.

The longer record is strong. HPE holds an RS rank of 96 of 99 on the desk's list and is up 133.5% this year. In the July quarter, EPS rose 404.8% to $1.06 and revenue climbed 33.7% to $12.21 billion. Per-share earnings across the four quarters given ran 0.11, 0.31, 0.44 and 1.06. The stock trades at 11.9 times forward earnings.
A headline Tuesday said HPE's Spaceborne Computer will power high performance computing and AI on the moon. Another asked why Wall Street won't touch a stock with a 12x forward P/E and 400% growth.
A close back above the 50-day line would repair part of the damage; a new base is needed before there is a fresh buy point.
article.watch: Whether Wednesday's session holds the after-hours gain and closes above the 50-day line at 59.45.

market_note: The Dow rose 1.0% to 52,495.88 and the S&P 500 added 0.3% to 7,712.57, while the Nasdaq finished flat at 26,424.82. The S&P 500 sits 0.1% above its 50-day line and the Dow 0.2% above, but the Nasdaq is 0.7% below it; the S&P 500 carries 5 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Dow 5 and the Nasdaq 2, and the desk's state is Uptrend under pressure. Leadership on the desk's list this week is oil: ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil, Chevron and EOG Resources all broke out of bases, joined by Pfizer, Mastercard and Berkshire Hathaway, while AI infrastructure lags with an average RS of 26 and only 12% of its names above the 50-day line. After hours, Super Micro Computer jumped 14.3%, Credo 9.3%, SpaceX 6.5%, Dell 6.0%, Nebius 5.7%, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Vertiv 5.4% each, while Intuitive Surgical fell 8.0% and Netflix 5.6%.
